center.locator: Arithmetic mean of the 275 unique vertices of the merged LHC ring (OSM relation 9512017)
center.note: Map centre only; not a claim about any structure. precision_m is set loosely (5 km) because this is a naive vertex-average centroid, not an area centroid.

depth_m.display: ≈78 m (56–100 m across the instrumented points)
depth_m.note: These are the four instrumented points' own surveyed/published depths, not the full ring's extreme range: no fetched source this session gives a whole-ring minimum/maximum depth (the often-quoted '45–170 m' figure appears only on secondary pages without an attributable primary citation, so it is not used here).
depth_m.quote: ALICE: 'The detector sits in a vast cavern 56 m below ground'; ATLAS and LHCb: 'sits in a cavern 100 m below ground' / 'sits 100 metres below ground'; CMS: '89 m below Earth's surface'; LHC ring generally: 'The accelerator sits in a tunnel 100 metres underground at CERN'.

levels.name: LHC/LEP tunnel and experiment caverns
levels.note: Plan view; depth varies with the Jura slope. Houses geometry:lhc-tunnel-ring, geometry:lep-tunnel-ring and the Point 1/2/5/8 boundaries and the CMS cavern point.

levels.name: SPS tunnel
levels.note: No fetched source states the SPS tunnel's depth below surface this session (left null per A17 rather than guessed).

levels.name: PS / PSB tunnels (shallow)
levels.note: No fetched source states the PS or PSB tunnel depth below surface this session (left null per A17 rather than guessed); both are shallower than the LHC/SPS tunnels per general CERN accelerator-chain descriptions, but that qualitative claim is not itself independently sourced here.

name: CERN — Meyrin, Prévessin and the LHC ring
notes: Linked maps: map:lngs (the CNGS far site at LNGS) does not exist yet in this atlas; linked_map_ids is left empty here and the build's automatic derivation (from beamline:cngs's far_detector_site_ids) will populate it once LNGS has its own map.

site:cern-lep-point-2-l3 and site:cern-point-2-alice, and site:cern-lep-point-8-delphi and site:cern-point-8-lhcb, are drawn as separate geometry features using the SAME underlying OSM polygon (the same physical Point 2 / Point 8 enclosure hosted a LEP experiment 1989-2000 and hosts an LHC experiment today); this is expected to raise the validator's geometry-duplicate-shape warning for those two pairs, documented here and in the worklog rather than avoided by omission.

Release pass (gaps stream, 2026-10-25): MapCERN's public Facilities layer (CERN GIS) names the SPS access buildings (868-873 = BA1-BA6), SR8 (2875), the HL-LHC buildings (SD/SE/SU/SF/SHM 17 and 57) and the ECN3 access and counting-room buildings (911, 918); the OpenStreetMap polygons carry those numbers, which is why the earlier name searches for UA1, UA2, CAST and ECN3 found nothing. UA1 and UA2 (underground in ECX5 and ECX4), CAST (SR8) and ECN3 (underground cavern, building 900) are therefore shown by the surface buildings that serve them, not by their own outlines; the HL-LHC surface buildings are drawn, its new shafts and galleries are not.

schematics.note: Official CERN Document Server diagram; topology only, not geographic. Never drawn on the to-scale map.
schematics.title: The CERN accelerator complex, layout in 2022 (schematic, not to scale)

summary.plain: CERN's main campus on the France-Switzerland border near Geneva: the 27-km LHC/LEP ring, the SPS, PS and PSB injector rings, and the surface sites of the ATLAS, CMS, ALICE and LHCb experiments, drawn to scale from OpenStreetMap and CERN's own published figures.
summary.technical: One local map for facility:cern spanning the Meyrin and Prévessin sites and the full LHC/LEP tunnel footprint. Geometry sourced from OpenStreetMap (relation 9512017 for the LHC/LEP ring; ways 66473762/174646428/309914733 for SPS/PS/PSB; named Point-N surface enclosures for ATLAS/ALICE/CMS/LHCb and their LEP-era predecessors L3/ALEPH/DELPHI) cross-checked against CERN's published circumference and depth figures, plus one CMS-paper surveyed cavern point and two ring-derived points for FASER/SND@LHC in TI12/TI18.

unlocated.backlog: A 1970s ISR design report or CERN historical civil-engineering plan with a scale bar, georeferenced against Meyrin buildings that still stand; the public MapCERN layers (Facilities, Levels, Rooms, surfaces) were searched this session and contain no ISR tunnel or building named as such.
unlocated.reason: The Intersecting Storage Rings occupied part of the Meyrin site until 1984. No OpenStreetMap trace was found this session (three Overpass name searches for 'ISR'/'Intersecting Storage' in the Meyrin bbox returned zero elements), and no other fetched source gives coordinates or a civil-engineering plan for its tunnel.

unlocated.backlog: A CERN document that gives the Linac2 building number (the TE-EPC Long Shutdown 2 page lists Meyrin-side building ranges 355-356, 361-363 and 365-367 without saying which is Linac2); once the number is known, MapCERN Facilities (https://maps.cern.ch/arcgis/rest/services/Hosted/Etages_v2_public/FeatureServer/114, field numero) gives its outline and the OSM way with that name gives a traced footprint.
unlocated.reason: Linac2 (in operation 1978-2018, switched off for the last time on 12 November 2018) has no OpenStreetMap building trace by name and no fetched CERN page gives a building number: the CERN Open Days page lists it only by a site-map grid reference ("ME.62", which is not a coordinate; the page returned HTTP 503 when re-fetched), and the public MapCERN layers carry building numbers and acronyms (Facilities) but no entry that names Linac2.
